Hi Maya —

Thanks for the note and the heads-up on your SIG timeline. High level: we perform a single security assessment that covers our managed control plane, public API endpoints, and the runtime components that live in Redwood-managed network segments. That assessment is what we typically provide to customers as "Redwood-managed scope."

Quick clarifications by hosting model:
- Hosted (Redwood API): included — control plane, public API surface, admin console, and runtime nodes are in-scope for our standard PT.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): included when the Dedicated pool is provisioned and managed by Redwood (we run the runtime and control plane). If you deploy Dedicated into a VarTech-managed network or bring-your-own-network configuration, that portion is out-of-scope.
- Private / VPC: split — Redwood-managed Private (we operate the control plane and provide connectors into your VPC) is included for the control plane and any Redwood-managed connector endpoints. Components that are installed inside your VPC and fully managed by you (customer agents, NAT, internal endpoints) are out of scope unless we run a scoped engagement.
- On-prem: generally out-of-scope — on-prem deployments where the customer runs the full stack are not covered by our standard assessment; we can perform a scoped engagement on request.

I'll attach a scope matrix that maps components to the standard assessment and note the typical exclusions. If it helps, can we set a 30-minute sync with our security lead to walk the auditor through the matrix? If so, please propose times.

Attaching: scope-matrix.xlsx (contains component-by-component matrix).

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Hi all —

Thanks for looping us in. Below are the concrete scope definitions we used for the January 2026 Redwood security assessment (redacted for customer sharing):

Scope included (Redwood-managed):
- Control plane services (auth, tenancy, admin console) accessible via API and web UI (hosted in our managed tenant environment).
- Runtime/model-serving nodes running in Redwood-managed clusters (both for Hosted and Dedicated capacity that we operate).
- Public API endpoints (token issuance, inference endpoints, streaming).
- Internal orchestration and build artifacts stored in Redwood-managed artifact stores referenced in the report.

Scope excluded (customer-managed / out-of-scope by default):
- Customer VPC resources (private subnets, customer-managed agents, on-prem gateways) unless a scoped engagement was purchased.
- Customer-managed Dedicated network attachments where the customer supplies their own network stack.
- On-prem full-stack installations (we can provide a separate engagement).

Dedicated specifics: the Dedicated pools that we provision and operate were included in the January 2026 test. Dedicated deployments where VarTech brings its own routing or NAT and we do not control the runtime networking were excluded.

Private / VPC specifics: when customers choose Redwood-managed Private (we operate the control plane and provide connector endpoints), the control plane and connector endpoints were included. Anything purely hosted inside your VPC that you manage (agents, internal-only endpoints) remained out-of-scope.

Attachments shared for VarTech (redacted copies):
- Redwood_PT_Report_Jan2026.pdf (redactions applied to internal hostnames and IPs)
- remediation-tracker.csv (current status by finding id)

Current remediation snapshot (high level):
- Critical: 1 finding (credential exposure) — fixed and validated (2026-02-10).
- High: 2 findings — 1 fixed, 1 mitigated in progress (ETA 2026-09-01).
- Medium: 6 findings — rolling fixes, majority scheduled during Aug/Sep maintenance windows.

Sharing notes: we can provide the redacted PT report and the remediation-tracker under an NDA or via your auditor portal. If your auditor requires the unredacted artifact, we'll need a formal request and an approved data sharing agreement.

If you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough, I can join Karthik and an auditor representative tomorrow 10–12 PT.

Regards,
